newsitem.title: USA: Police question suspects in murder of Chinese girl.
newsitem.headline: Police question suspects in murder of Chinese girl.

text.p: Police are questioning several men in connection with the murder of an 11-year-old Chinese girl who came to the United States last year, authorities said on Friday.

The body of fifth grader Quin-Rong Wu, who vanished two weeks ago in New York after kissing her mother goodbye less than a block from her Chinatown school, was found strangled and floating in Manhattan's East River on Wednesday, police said.
The severely decomposed corpse was identified using dental X-rays, medical examiners said.
Wu, who knew only a little English, was reported missing on May 13 after she failed to return home, police said.
On Tuesday, police released a sketch of a man they were seeking in connection with the girl's disappearance.

A woman reported last weekend that she saw a girl fitting Wu's description with the profiled man in the subway, an hour after she said goodbye to her mother. She was crying and looking lost, the woman said.
Local radio reports claimed that one of the men police were questioning on Friday was a homeless man who looked like the person on the police posters.
A police spokesman said there was no one suspect, but rather several men who had been picked up for questioning.
Police Commissioner Howard Safir said the city was offering a $10,000 reward for information leading to the case being solved.
